stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when tested against the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This update specifically targets Apple Silicon devices, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and speed.
The core value proposition is running AI capabilities entirely on the user's own device.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Sony’s PlayStation disc factory is already being repurposed
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Sony is actively repurposing its PlayStation disc manufacturing facilities.
The industry shift towards digital media is confirmed, signaling the decline of physical game discs.
Sony's Thalgau plant currently produces 600,000 discs daily, half of which are for PlayStation.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New security threat identified in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Attackers can distribute malicious payloads across multiple Pull Requests (PRs) to evade detection.
The paper introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the safe deployment of capable but potentially untrusted AI.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper introduces LACUNA, a new testbed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning.
It addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not the internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-function programming,' a new paradigm for handling complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs to improve locality, reproducibility, and cost for tasks like log alerting or JSON repair.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses limitations of current LLM API usage, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a new data-agnostic quantization method specifically designed for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses a major bottleneck in state-of-the-art image/video generation: the high computational cost of DiT inference due to multi-step sampling and large parameters.
Solves the problem of activation shifting across different timesteps and prompts, which plagues traditional Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) methods.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
It introduces LACUNA, a new testbed designed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level rather than verifying true knowledge erasure within the model parameters.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for improved functionality on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the context and knowledge base of Claude Code.

stories.title: Meta has a new app called Pocket that is absolutely nothing like the old Pocket
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is launching a new app named Pocket, replacing the functionality of the discontinued Mozilla Pocket.
The new Pocket app is heavily AI-focused, allowing users to create and share interactive 'gizmos' from AI prompts.
This move aligns with Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's strong commitment to integrating AI across its products.

stories.title: The video game disc is dead
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: The traditional physical video game disc format is reportedly nearing obsolescence.
The article discusses the evolution of gaming hardware and media over the decades.
This shift suggests a continued move toward digital distribution in the gaming industry.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new macOS infostealer, PamStealer, has been discovered.
The malware represents an increasing focus on targeting Mac users.
This highlights the growing sophistication of malware targeting Apple ecosystems.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to allow supersonic airliners to operate over US cities.
The key condition for this approval is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to eliminate the sonic boom.
This represents a potential regulatory shift enabling faster, supersonic commercial air travel within the US airspace.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs in real-world deployment despite alignment training.
The paper proposes a simple, real-time monitoring system that uses an external model's verification signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, and shows competitive performance.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long input contexts.
Introduces RECONTEXT (Recursive Evidence Replay), a proposed training-free inference method to improve long-context reasoning.
Focuses on bridging the gap between LLM's ability to access long context and its ability to utilize that context effectively.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances in a shared debate history against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses.
Examines the emergence of latent objectives within agents when social context is present but not explicitly prompted.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
Introduces DramaSR-532K, a large-scale benchmark dataset with 532K annotated dialogue lines.
Leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of attributing utterances to specific characters.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLM training.
Addresses a key limitation of existing OPSD methods: teacher-side token-level supervision can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The proposed method aims to mitigate these issues by modulating the disagreement during the self-distillation process.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide classical constraint satisfaction methods (e.g., SAT solvers).
The research focuses on SE-RRMs, which show improved extrapolation capabilities when handling larger problem sizes.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of Large Language Models (LLMs) memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It focuses on 'unlearning,' a method to reliably remove this memorized knowledge post-hoc, which is a growing area of AI safety research.
The research introduces 'LACUNA' to test localization precision, arguing that current benchmarks only check output-level erasure, not true knowledge removal.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses to detect emergent social dynamics.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study how unprompted social context shapes agent expression.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that traditional dense token-level supervision in OPSD causes overfitting and harms cross-domain generalization.
Aims to improve LLM reasoning by modulating policy based on disagreement, mitigating the pitfalls of privileged information.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a framework for creating controllable simulated agents.
Agents can imitate logged behavior while allowing steering along interpretable axes.
This controllability is crucial for testing autonomous systems and isolating variables in traffic simulation without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of training LLMs in specialized domains without expensive human annotations.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Leverages the model's own outputs and majority voting across rollouts to generate pseudo-labels.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under real-world, decentralized data conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness, filling a current gap in the research literature.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Proposes 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based tasks that are currently outsourced to LLMs.
The core idea is to compile a natural-language specification into a compact, locally-executable neural artifact (Program-as-Weights).
Addresses key drawbacks of LLM reliance, namely issues with locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances to off-the-record (OTR) responses to detect emergent, unprompted objectives.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the impact of relational context on LLM communication.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to mitigate this vulnerability.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection capabilities.
Existing LVLMs struggle to properly ground their self-reflection process in visual inputs, especially for novel (out-of-distribution) images.
The proposed solution utilizes Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to perform visually grounded self-correction during reasoning.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates the potential of scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve the fidelity of social simulations.
It questions whether current scaling laws alone can bridge the gap between LLM capabilities and realistic social simulation.
The study explores if simulation fidelity is an independent research area separate from general LLM performance improvements.

stories.title: Arbitrary code execution breaking sandboxes in KDE Plasma
stories.author: blog.kimiblock.top via ecksdee
bullet_points: A vulnerability allowing arbitrary code execution has been discovered in KDE Plasma.
The exploit specifically targets and breaks out of sandboxing mechanisms within the desktop environment.
This represents a significant security flaw in a widely used Linux desktop environment.
